This test plan incorporated parametric testing for MEA and ICE-21™ solvents to act as a baseline before transitioning to the ICE-31® test campaign. The key performance indicators for this testing included, but were not limited to emission rates, solvent stability, capture efficiencies, and cooling requirements. ION Clean Energy 10 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 4.5.1 MEA Baseline ION performed baseline testing of the NGCC engineering scale system with the 1st generation solvent, MEA. The performance metrics obtained while using this solvent for baseline performance of the engineering scale system were compared to well-known systems worldwide. 4.5.2 ICE-21™ Baseline ION performed the testing of the NGCC engineering scale system with the 2nd generation solvent, ICE-21™. The parametric testing demonstrated how this solvent compares to the performance metrics from the MEA baseline. These data were also compared to the ICE-31® performance metrics. 4.5.3 ICE-31® Campaign ION performed the testing of the NGCC engineering scale system with the 3rd generation solvent, ICE-31®. This solvent underwent a parametric testing phase to generate performance metrics for direct comparison to the MEA and ICE-21™ baselines. Subsequently, the solvent underwent long- term testing to determine its composition over time, including degradation products, and to assess the makeup solvent or reclamation needs necessary to maintain solvent performance. A long testing period between February 2024 and February 2025 was completed to optimize and validate the solvent maintenance strategy, given the enhanced oxidative stability of ICE-31®. 4.6 Decommissioning of 1 MWe (10 tpd) NGCC Engineering Scale System ION decommissioned the system at the end of the testing campaign and will proceed with the disposition according to the Cooperative Agreement. 4.7 Data Analysis and Final Reporting ION documented the results of the design, construction, and testing phases of the project and generated a comprehensive account for the work performed through the quarterly reports and various communications with the DOE, including the NETL conferences. ION Clean Energy 11 DE-FE0031950: FINAL PROJECT REPORT 5 Budget Period 1 – Technical Overview In Budget Period 1, ION collaborated with the project team to develop the engineering package for a firm, fixed-price proposal to fabricate and install the modules as well as the BOP systems. In support of the engineering package, the team developed P&IDs, a general 3D-layout, and a detailed HAZOP study. The phase concluded with design packages, a fixed price cost to be compared against the budget, and an executed Host Site Agreement.
